title: San'yō in 6 Days — Hiroshima, Miyajima, Onomichi, Kurashiki, Okayama
subtitle: In and out of Okayama: one night in Kurashiki, three in Hiroshima, then Onomichi on the way back to Okayama
summary: In and out of Okayama Momotaro Airport: day 1 to Kurashiki, then three nights in Hiroshima for Miyajima, the Atomic Bomb Dome and Kure, day 5 round by Onomichi back to Okayama, and Okayama Castle and Kōraku-en to finish. Travel on day 5 (Onomichi and the changes) takes over a third of the day; for an easier trip, drop what follows lunch in Onomichi. Tomonoura, Fukuyama Castle and Kibitsu Shrine are held as alternates.

Could not be confirmed from official sources — check before you go

Opening hours for Achi Shrine, the shops in the Kurashiki Bikan quarter, the Hiroshima Castle keep (9:00–18:00 from the 2023 travel log's notice board), Itsukushima Shrine's visiting hours and fee (about ¥300), the JMSDF Kure Museum, the Onomichi shops, Hiroshima Okonomi-monogatari, Kakiya and AEON Mall Okayama.
The ¥100 Miyajima visitor tax: 2023 travel log information, not found on the official site.
The current one-way Shinkansen fare between Okayama and Hiroshima.
Changes and trade-offs

The travel log began and ended in Hiroshima (in fact flying in and out of Okayama, with a train to Hiroshima on day 1 and back to Okayama on the last day); this one is in and out of Okayama and reordered: Kurashiki moved to day 1, three nights in Hiroshima, Onomichi on the way back to Okayama on day 5, and Okayama Castle and Kōraku-en split across days 5 and 6.
The log's Fukuyama, Tomonoura, Sensui-jima, Kibitsu Shrine and small Kurashiki shops are held as alternates.
On day 5 travel to and from Onomichi and the changes take more than 30% of the day; this is the move day between Hiroshima and Okayama; for an easier day, drop what follows lunch in Onomichi.
The log's author travelled alone; the template is arranged for 2 adults, with a more relaxed pace.
Transport tickets

Okayama–Hiroshima–Yamaguchi Area Pass (JR West): 5 consecutive days, ¥17,000 for adults (as shown on the official site; prices may change), covering the San'yō Shinkansen between Okayama and Hakata (reserved seats), JR conventional lines and the JR Miyajima ferry. On this itinerary the pass starts when you take JR from Okayama Station to Kurashiki on day 1, and days 1–5 use it fully; the airport bus on day 6 is not covered.

Without the pass, the 2023 travel log's figures: Okayama ↔ Hiroshima one way by Shinkansen is about ¥6,460, and with the Miyajima, Onomichi and Kure round trips the pass is better value; work it out against the fares before you go.
The Hiroden streetcar is a flat ¥240 in the city, paid when you get off; the Miyajima visitor tax is ¥100 per person, bought on the island at Miyajimaguchi pier with staff to guide you.
Okayama Momotaro Airport to and from the city

Airport bus to Okayama Station: about 30 min, ¥1,000 from the west exit of Okayama Station (¥950 from Undōkōen-mae and Okayama Daigaku-dōri); transit IC cards such as ICOCA and Suica are accepted; the timetable is valid 25 Oct 2026–31 Jan 2027.

After international arrivals from Taipei and Kaohsiung there are extra buses towards Okayama Station that are not in the timetable; go straight to the stop after customs and queue; the 2023 travel log says it leaves when full.

Airport direct to Kurashiki Station: about 35 min, ¥1,400; 12 services leave the airport, 5 of them daily and the rest only on certain dates, and 9 daily services run from Kurashiki to the airport. Check the official site for times.
Back to the airport on day 6: take the same airport bus from the west exit of Okayama Station; the travel log says it is crowded before international departures but extra buses run.
Official site: https://www.okayama-airport.org/tw/access/bus
Accommodation

Night 1 in Kurashiki: the log's author stayed at HOTEL LiVEMAX Okayama Kurashiki-Ekimae, about 5 min on foot outside Kurashiki Station; the log says it has no 24-hour desk, so be back before the desk closes.

Nights 2–4 in Hiroshima: the log's author stayed at Toyoko Inn Hiroshima-eki Stadium-mae, outside Mazda Stadium; it is about 15 min on foot from the station, across a level crossing; the room faces the railway and you hear trains pass.
Night 5 in Okayama: stay around Okayama Station and take the airport bus straight from there the next day.
Weather and season

In mid to late November Okayama Kōraku-en and Okayama Castle have autumn illuminations (check the Okayama tourism site for dates); when the log's author visited in November, Hiroshima was about 4°C at night, so bring warm clothes.

Low tide at Itsukushima Shrine differs every day; if you want to photograph the shrine and torii at low tide, look up the tide table first; when the log's author visited in November, low tide was around 3 a.m. and 5 p.m.
Booking and reminders
On day 2 the Atomic Bomb museum needs an online reservation for 7:30–8:30 and some evening slots; ordinary daytime slots do not.
The Yamato Museum is closed Tuesdays, so day 4 can be swapped around by day of the week.
You cannot bring your own food on Tigerair (per the travel log), and meat products must not be brought into Japan.
Carry yen in cash and a transit IC card.
Alternates
Tomonoura, Fukuyama Castle, Kibitsu Shrine and the small Kurashiki shops are held as alternates, to add depending on time and weather.

notes.title: Trip overview: how the 6 days run
paragraphs: In and out of Okayama Momotaro Airport: the first night in Kurashiki, then three nights with Hiroshima as the base, and the last night back in Okayama. The Sanyo Shinkansen and JR are the spine, with the tram inside Hiroshima and the JR Miyajima ferry for the island.
Day 1: land in the afternoon, take the airport bus and JR to Kurashiki, visit Achi Shrine in the evening, stroll the {@d1-03}, and have dinner near Kurashiki Station.
Day 2: JR and the Shinkansen to Hiroshima, then the {@d2-01} and the Peace Memorial Museum, okonomiyaki for lunch, Hiroshima Castle in the afternoon and {@d2-05} towards evening.
Day 3: all day on Miyajima for {@d3-01} and a lunch of oysters, then the {@d3-03} in the afternoon, and dinner near Hiroshima Station.
Day 4: the JR Kure Line to Kure for the {@d4-01} and the JMSDF Kure Museum, Kure cold noodles for lunch, and shopping at Hiroshima Station in the evening.
Day 5: head from Hiroshima towards Okayama, stopping in Onomichi for {@d5-01} and Onomichi ramen, then drop your bags in Okayama and see {@d5-03} in the evening.
Day 6: {@d6-01} in the morning, souvenirs at {@d6-02} and tempura soba for lunch, then the airport bus from the west exit of the station back to the airport.
Where to sleep: the first night near Kurashiki Station, nights 2 to 4 near Hiroshima Station, and the fifth night in front of Okayama Station, with the airport bus the next morning.

Getting around: the airport bus takes about 30 minutes to Okayama Station, and some departures run straight to Kurashiki Station; between Okayama, Kurashiki, Hiroshima, Onomichi and Kure it is JR and the Sanyo Shinkansen, so work out whether the JR West Okayama-Hiroshima-Yamaguchi Area Pass pays off at current prices; inside Hiroshima ride the Hiroden tram; for Miyajima take the JR ferry, and a separate visitor tax applies on the island. On day 5 more than a third of the time goes on transit to and from Onomichi, so if you want an easier day, drop what comes after the Onomichi lunch. Check the latest timetables before you go.

Who it suits: anyone who wants to fly in and out of Okayama and link Kurashiki, Hiroshima, Miyajima, Kure, Onomichi and Okayama in one trip, paced for two adults. The days involve a lot of walking, so wear comfortable shoes, and leave extra time on day 2, because the museum is heavy going.
